result.source: Restaurant Mon Ami, Trg kralja Tomislava 26, Velika Gorica (Croatia). Investigated: Gault&Millau Croatia listing (hr.gaultmillau.com, including raw JSON-LD structured data for exact score/toques), MICHELIN Guide restaurant listing + MICHELIN Guide editorial feature (Oct 2025, Sarah Scaparone), Visit Zagreb County (HR + EN), Tjedan restorana HR (HR + EN), the restaurant's own site monami.hr/o-nama (raw HTML scraped for verbatim Croatian), Okusi hrvatske tradicije (okusi.hr), Gastronaut.hr, PutniKofer.hr gastro feature, Eat Out Zagreb review (Sept 2023), Kronike Velike Gorice / velikagorica.com / rvg.hr / 01portal.hr news archives, Restaurant Guru and TripAdvisor aggregates.
result.summary:
Mon Ami is a family-run Mediterranean/seafood restaurant in the centre of Velika Gorica, open since 1997 and still run by the Ceronja family — today by Bruno Ceronja, son of the founders, alongside his mother Barica (referred to as Barbara in one source). The founding couple combined their roots: the father was from the Skradin area, the mother a native Turopoljka, so they put Dalmatian fish cooking and continental Turopolje dishes under one roof — near-avant-garde for a town that ate grilled meat. Bruno describes the ambition as uniting "dvije kuhinje pod istim krovom, onu mediteransku i kontinentalnu" and calls his father's turn to fish "prava mala revolucija".

The kitchen is led by chef Goran Marko Beus, 45, a Split native who built his career on the Dalmatian coast and on ships; he has run the pass for roughly 16-17 years. Signature dishes: crni rižoto od sipe (black cuttlefish risotto, the best-known), octopus salad, smoked Pag mussels, tuna carpaccio with Turopolje black truffle, Kvarner scampi, dry-aged local beef (a 45-day dry-aged Posavina T-bone), grilled salmon with teriyaki and celery purée, skradinska torta and hazelnut/white chocolate semifreddo.

Two distinct guide recognitions are confirmed. Gault&Millau Croatia 2026: 13.5/20 and 2 toques (verified in the page's JSON-LD: "2 toques Gault&Millau (2026)"), chef listed as Marko Beus, head sommelier Zlatko Šimac. MICHELIN: recommended/Selected since 2018 and continuously thereafter (third year in 2020, fourth in 2021, sixth by 2023, retained for 2025 at the Šibeniks St. John Fortress ceremony, and again in the 2026 guide), price band €€€, Mediterranean. It also holds Restaurant Croatica 2024 (100 leading Croatian restaurants, 30th edition presented on botel Marina in Rijeka), has been in Croatia's top-100 list 23 times (1999-2002, 2004-2008, 2010-2012, 2015-2025), holds a Green Destination certificate and a Zagreb County award for sustainable restaurant, plus the "Okusi tradicije Zagrebačkog kraja" plaque.

House specialities include their own gold-medal extra virgin olive oil from the family olive grove in Skradin (mostly oblica; 10th place with 96.42 points and a gold at Dani mladih maslinovih ulja in Vodice), Croatian green olives, olive tea, and a house cuvée Chardonnay-Graševina from the Pokuplje sub-region, Vukomeričke gorice, on a 60-label list (the restaurant's own site says 60; Gastronaut lists 65).

facts.label: Founding year
facts.value: 1997 — "nudi svoj bogati opus jela i pića od 1997. godine" (restaurant's own Tjedan restorana text); confirmed by MICHELIN Guide, PutniKofer and multiple news sources. NOTE: one 2020 Kronike VG article says the family restaurant opened in 1994 and had run 25 years — treat 1997 as the canonical year.

facts.label: Family / ownership
facts.value: Founded and still run by the Ceronja family. Owner: Barica Ceronja (one review names her Barbara). Manager/director: Bruno Ceronja, son of the founders. Father Božo was from the Skradin area, mother a native Turopoljka. After the father's death Bruno took over management with his mother.

facts.label: Chef
facts.value: Goran Marko Beus (listed by Gault&Millau simply as Marko Beus), aged 45, born in Split, career built along the Dalmatian coast and working on ships. MICHELIN (Oct 2025) says seventeen years leading the kitchen; PutniKofer says sixteen; Eat Out Zagreb (2023) said fifteen.

facts.label: Head sommelier
facts.value: Zlatko Šimac (per Gault&Millau structured data)

facts.label: Gault&Millau score
facts.value: 13.5/20 (bestRating 20, worstRating 1), Gault&Millau Croatia 2026 edition, review published 7 May 2026

facts.label: Gault&Millau toques
facts.value: 2 toques — exact value from the page's JSON-LD: "Distinction Gault&Millau" = "2 toques Gault&Millau (2026)"; page GTM payload also carries "toques":2

facts.label: Gault&Millau category
facts.value: Listed as "Chef's Restaurant"; cuisine classified as Seafood

facts.label: MICHELIN status
facts.value: MICHELIN Guide recommended / Selected (no star, no Bib Gourmand). Cuisine: Mediterranean. Price band: €€€. Tagged "Family Friendly".

facts.label: MICHELIN — first recommendation
facts.value: 2018. The inspector dined anonymously and revealed himself only after paying the bill.

facts.label: MICHELIN — consecutive years
facts.value: 3rd consecutive year reported May 2020; 4th reported Oct 2021; 6th consecutive by Sept 2023; retained in MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2025 (ceremony at Tvrđava sv. Ivana, Šibenik, July 2025); again in MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2026 (reported 25 June 2026)

facts.label: MICHELIN — county exclusivity
facts.value: Until 2021 Mon Ami was the only restaurant in the whole of Zagreb County with MICHELIN status. In the 2026 guide, Zagreb County also has Korak (1 star) and newcomer Cantilly Garden (MICHELIN Selected).

facts.label: MICHELIN editorial feature
facts.value: Full MICHELIN Guide article "Mon Ami, Zagreb County, Croatia: Where tradition meets land and sea", published 6 October 2025, written by Sarah Scaparone (sponsored content in collaboration with Croatia)

facts.label: Restaurant Croatica award
facts.value: Restaurant Croatica 2024 — included among the 100 leading Croatian restaurants. Presented in the 30th edition of the book "Restaurant Croatica – 100 vodećih hrvatskih restorana i njihovi specijaliteti 2025/26", at a ceremony on botel Marina in Rijeka (reported 27 September 2025). The award has run since 1995, based on guest votes, hospitality-professional recommendations and a final decision by the project's Časni odbor.

facts.label: Top-100 Croatian restaurants count
facts.value: Named among Croatia's top 100 restaurants 23 times: 1999-2002, 2004-2008, 2010-2012 and 2015-2025 (per Gastronaut.hr)

facts.label: Sustainability awards
facts.value: Green Destination certificate and a Zagreb County award for sustainable restaurant — confirmed by Bruno Ceronja: "Imamo Green Destination certifikat i nagradu Zagrebačke županije za održivi restoran." Exact award year not published.

facts.label: Other recognition
facts.value: Plaque "Okusi tradicije Zagrebačkog kraja" (partner of the Okusi hrvatske tradicije programme); TripAdvisor recommendation cited on the restaurant's own site

facts.label: Olive grove — location
facts.value: The family's own olive grove is in Skradin (Dalmatian hinterland, Šibenik-Knin County), the father's home region. Mostly the oblica variety. Described as domaće, ekološko maslinovo ulje.

facts.label: Olive oil — gold medal
facts.value: Extra virgin olive oil "nagrađivano zlatnim medaljama" (gold medals, plural, cited across all official listings). Specific result: 10th place with 96.42 points and a gold award (zlatno odličje) for young olive oil at the national Dani mladih maslinovih ulja event in Vodice.

facts.label: Olive oil — role in the kitchen
facts.value: Chef Beus calls the Skradin oil the foundation of everything — he cannot imagine the kitchen without it, and defines Mediterranean cooking as quality oil, fresh fruit and vegetables, and minimal thermal processing. The team joins the olive and grape harvests together.

facts.label: Olive products sold
facts.value: Croatian green olives (hrvatske zelene masline) and olive tea (čaj od maslina) are sold alongside the oil

facts.label: House wine
facts.value: Own house wine: cuvée Chardonnay Graševina from the Pokuplje sub-region, Vukomeričke gorice vinogorje

facts.label: Wine list size
facts.value: 60 labels ("vinska karta od 60 etiketa, poglavito vina hrvatskih proizvođača") per the restaurant's own About page, Visit Zagreb County and okusi.hr. Gastronaut.hr lists 65 labels — likely a more recent count.

facts.label: Capacity — total
facts.value: 70 seats total per the restaurant's own site and Tjedan restorana. MICHELIN (2025) describes roughly sixty indoors plus about twenty on the terrace. Okusi.hr lists 60 indoor + 10 meeting room.

facts.label: Capacity — private room
facts.value: A separate "separe" for 10 people, intended for closed-type business meetings ("poslovnim sastancima zatvorenog tipa")

facts.label: Terrace
facts.value: Enclosed/covered and heated terrace, approx. 40 m2 with five tables seating around 20 guests, built c. 2021-2022. Gault&Millau notes the closed terrace has a slightly more casual atmosphere than the white-tablecloth formal room.

facts.label: Interior
facts.value: Built from natural materials reflecting the owners' approach to living and business. MICHELIN describes regional oak tabletops plus marble and stone. Divided into two parts: formal room with white tablecloths, and the closed terrace.

facts.label: Events — business, weddings, sacraments
facts.value: The restaurant markets itself for "poslovna druženja, svadbe, pričesti, krizme i krštenja" (business gatherings, weddings, first communions, confirmations, christenings). Also runs themed dinners and days devoted to local seasonal ingredients ("tematske večere i dane posvećene domaćim sezonskim namirnicama").

facts.label: Business lunches
facts.value: On weekdays the clientele skews to business people and travellers in transit due to airport proximity; weekends it becomes a family destination. The 10-seat separe is explicitly for closed business meetings.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Parking available. Okusi.hr lists parking capacity as 5 and 15 (two lots/figures). Restaurant Guru lists Parking: yes. Reviews note ample parking space; nearby are the bus station, the municipality building, Muzej Turopolja, Zagrebačka banka and Fina. A park with a playground sits in front of the restaurant.

facts.label: Zagreb Airport proximity
facts.value: Located in central Velika Gorica in the immediate vicinity of Franjo Tuđman International Airport (Pleso). The restaurant's own text positions it for everyone "od usputnog prolaznika do putnika koji između dva leta želi nešto dobro pojesti" — from the passer-by to the traveller who wants something good to eat between two flights. Tjedan restorana describes it as being on the road toward Sisak or Zračna luka «Pleso».

facts.label: Address
facts.value: Trg kralja Tomislava 26, 10410 Velika Gorica, Croatia

facts.label: Phone
facts.value: +385 1 6213 333 (written locally as 01 6213 333)

facts.label: Email
facts.value: monamihr@gmail.com

facts.label: Website and socials
facts.value: https://www.monami.hr/ ; Facebook /monamihr ; Instagram /restoranmonami

facts.label: Opening hours
facts.value: Monday 11:00-16:30; Tuesday-Saturday 11:00-23:00; Sunday closed. Gastronaut also notes annual closure 1-21 August.

facts.label: Accessibility
facts.value: Accessible for people with disabilities (Gault&Millau amenity flag; okusi.hr confirms accessible entry). Air conditioning per MICHELIN. WiFi available per okusi.hr.

facts.label: Payment
facts.value: Credit cards accepted — Maestro, Visa, MasterCard, Diners Club (Gastronaut). Okusi.hr lists cash and Maestro.

facts.label: House rules
facts.value: Reservations advised, advance notice for larger groups; no smoking; no pets (okusi.hr)

facts.label: Turopolje black truffle
facts.value: Fresh native black Turopolje truffle (crni turopoljski tartuf) served daily, year-round; white truffles used seasonally. Sourced through a truffle hunter trained in Istria. The restaurant switched from Istrian to local Turopolje truffles. Guests can order a day ahead to buy and grate fresh truffle themselves.

facts.label: Local sourcing
facts.value: Most ingredients travel under 100 km — "Sve što može biti lokalno koristimo u kuhinji." Named suppliers: honey from OPG Balić (Žumberak Highlands), hazelnuts and hazelnut paste from OPG Haha (Turopolje), Turopolje pears from OPG Goga. Menu changes seasonally (asparagus and strawberries, then pumpkin and porcini).

facts.label: Made in-house
facts.value: Bread, gnocchi and croquettes are all made in-house

facts.label: Motto / slogan
facts.value: "Restoran Mon Ami, za vas...kao prijatelj prijatelju." (for you... as a friend to a friend)

facts.label: Ratings aggregate
facts.value: TripAdvisor 4.7/5 from ~99-100 reviews, ranked #1 of 21 restaurants in Velika Gorica. Google 4.8/5 from ~1,445 reviews. Facebook 4.9/5 from 69 reviews. Restaurant Guru 4.8/5, #1 of 59 in Velika Gorica, 1,635 votes total.

facts.label: Price per person (informal)
facts.value: Restaurant Guru reports roughly €10-15 to €15-20 per person from reviewers; MICHELIN places it in the €€€ band. Not an official price list.

verbatimCroatian: Neka Vaša nepca dožive jedinstveni gastronomski užitak mediteranskih specijaliteta u srcu Turopolja.
Kušajte naše delicije poput kvarnerskih škampi, jastoga, školjki, carpaccia od tune s crnim tartufom ili gavuna prženih na maslinovom ulju.
U Mon Amiju vas očekuje dnevno svježa i divlja bijela riba, crni rižoto od sipe, jadranska lignja i hobotnica na salatu, dimljene dagnje.
Uz morska jela možete uživati i u beefsteaku s roštilja u umaku od tartufate i crnog tartufa. Također, nudimo vegetarijanska i jela bez glutena.
Kušajte naše extra djevičansko maslinovo ulje iz vlastitog maslinika u Skradinu, nagrađivano zlatnim medaljama. Shodno tome u ponudi imamo hrvatske zelene masline, te čaj od maslina.
Imamo vinsku kartu od 60 etiketa, poglavito vina hrvatskih proizvođača. Također proizvodimo svoje vino kuće cuvee Chardonnay Graševina iz podregije Pokuplje, vinogorje Vukomeričke gorice.

Organiziramo tematske večere i dane posvećene domaćim sezonskim namirnicama. Restoran ima 70 sjedećih mjesta. Odvojeni „separe“ za 10 osoba namijenjen je poslovnim sastancima zatvorenog tipa. Interijer je sadržan od prirodnih materijala koji predstavljaju naš pristup življenju i poslovanju.
Imamo preporuku od Croatia Michelin Restaurants – The Michelin Guide i Trip Advisora, a naša najvažnija preporuka su naši gosti.
Prepustite se našem osoblju koje će vas oduševiti svojom kreativnošću i ljubaznošću.
Restoran Mon Ami na putu prema Sisku ili Zračnoj luci «Pleso» u centru Velike Gorice na adresi Trg kralja Tomislava 26 nudi svoj bogati opus jela i pića od 1997. godine.

Tijekom godine u mogućnosti ste doživjeti ugođaj Prokljana i Jadranskog akvatorija poput kvarnerskih škampi, jastoga, školjki, carpaccia od tune s crnim tartufom ili gavuna prženih na maslinovom ulju.
Restoran Mon Ami omogućuje 70 sjedećih mjesta, od toga 10 u zasebnom «separeu» prikladnom za druženja ili sastanke zatvorenog tipa.
Restoran Mon Ami, za vas...kao prijatelj prijatelju.
Ne biste očekivali kvalitetan riblji restoran starog kova u Velikoj Gorici, ali upravo to dobit ćete u elegantnom restoranu Mon Ami.
Osim jadranskih, tu su i klasični kontinentalni specijaliteti, a dugu tradiciju i kvalitetu vodič Michelin nagradio je preporukom.

U ponudi imaju extra djevičansko maslinovo ulje iz vlastitog maslinika u Skradinu, nagrađivano zlatnim medaljama, hrvatske zelene masline te čaj od maslina. Također, proizvode i svoje vino kuće cuvee Chardonnay Graševina iz podregije Pokuplje i imaju vinsku kartu od 60 etiketa, poglavito hrvatskih proizvođača.
Neka vaša nepca dožive jedinstveni gastronomski užitak mediteranskih specijaliteta u srcu Turopolja.
Tradicija duga 25 godina.
Tri godine zaredom Restoran Mon Ami ima Michelinovu preporuku.
Restoran Mon Ami idealno je mjesto za poslovna druženja, svadbe, pričesti, krizme i krštenja.

gaps: NO Tjedan restorana fixed menu exists. I scraped the raw HTML of both the Croatian and English Tjedan restorana pages — the 'JELOVNIK' section is structurally present but completely empty: 'Cijena ručka: €' and 'Cijena večere: €' have no values, and the 'PRINT VERZIJA' PDF link has an empty href (href=""). There are no courses, no predjelo/glavno/desert breakdown, and no prices. The only usable data is the participation window: 21.3.-30.3.2025, with lunch and dinner. Do not expect a Tjedan restorana tasting menu for this restaurant.

The only dish prices I could verify anywhere are from the Eat Out Zagreb review of September 2023 (carpaccio €16, smoked mussels €12, scampi €80/kg, squid €53/kg, tenderloin €29). These are three years old and should be treated as indicative, not current. No current official price list is published online.

Gault&Millau: I confirmed 13.5/20 and 2 toques for the 2026 edition from the page's JSON-LD, but only the ENGLISH review text is published. The Croatian-language version of the Gault&Millau review returns HTTP 404 at both /hr/restorani/mon-ami and /restorani/mon-ami — so the Gault&Millau review cannot be quoted in Croatian.

Founding year conflict: nearly all sources say 1997, but a Kronike Velike Gorice article from May 2020 states the family restaurant opened in 1994 and had been running 25 years. I could not resolve which is correct; 1997 is far better attested and appears in the restaurant's own copy.

Michelin consecutive-year count is not stated as a single authoritative number. I could verify: first recommendation 2018, '3rd year running' (2020), '4th year running' (2021), '6th consecutive' (2023), retained 2025, listed again 2026. Nobody publishes an explicit 'eighth year in a row' claim, so avoid asserting a specific ordinal for 2026.
Wine list size conflicts: the restaurant's own site, Visit Zagreb County and okusi.hr all say 60 labels; Gastronaut.hr says 65. The 60 figure is what the restaurant itself publishes.

Capacity figures conflict mildly: restaurant's own site and Tjedan say 70 total (10 in the separe); MICHELIN says ~60 indoors plus ~20 on the terrace (i.e. ~80); okusi.hr says 60 indoor + 10 meeting room. Likely 70 indoors including the separe, plus ~20 on the enclosed terrace.
Chef's tenure conflicts: 15 years (2023), 16 years (2025 PutniKofer), 17 years (2025 MICHELIN). Implies he started around 2008-2010.

Owner's first name conflicts: Gastronaut and most sources say Barica Ceronja; the Eat Out Zagreb review calls her Barbara and names the late founder Božo. Bruno Ceronja's name is consistent everywhere.

Parking is confirmed to exist (Restaurant Guru flag, okusi.hr lists capacities '5' and '15', reviews mention ample space) but there is no authoritative statement of how many spaces are reserved for the restaurant, or whether parking is free or dedicated.

No confirmation of a dedicated wedding/banquet menu, maximum wedding party size, or event pricing. The restaurant advertises 'svadbe, pričesti, krizme i krštenja' but with only 70 seats, large weddings would need direct confirmation.

The exact year of the Zagreb County 'sustainable restaurant' award is not published — only Bruno Ceronja's statement that they hold it. Similarly, the year of the 'Okusi tradicije Zagrebačkog kraja' plaque is unstated.

The olive oil's specific gold-medal competition results beyond the Vodice 'Dani mladih maslinovih ulja' result (10th place, 96.42 points, gold) are not detailed anywhere — sources only say 'nagrađivano zlatnim medaljama' in the plural.

Image licensing: the PutniKofer photos are credited to Krešimir Čižmek / Putni Kofer and the restaurant's private archive; the Eat Out Zagreb photos are marked all rights reserved; the Gault&Millau photos are credited to Jakob Goldstein. None of these are free to reuse on a commercial website without permission. The Visit Zagreb County and the restaurant's own monami.hr images are the more defensible sources, but still require clearance.
Michelin's editorial feature was published as SPONSORED content in collaboration with the Croatian National Tourist Board — worth knowing before citing it as independent critical judgement.

The monami.hr homepage is essentially empty (navigation and footer only) and the site footer still reads 'Copyright © 2020', suggesting the site is not actively maintained; the 'Tradicija duga 25 godina' line on the About page is therefore stale (it would be ~29 years as of 2026).
